Part I — Knowledge Base (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Knowledge Base (Session 79, English)
A Live Kul Devta Roll Call: Identifying Family/Ancestral Deities, "T arang" Readings, and Why Kul Devta Must Never Be Forgotten

Sour ce: a live Ashaeiynn "Kul Devta Session" — a dedicated session (prioritized this week ahead of continuing the Chandravanshi series) devoted to identifying individual practitioners' kul devta/kul devi (family or ancestral deity), consisting almost entir ely of live, one-on-one exchanges with dozens of named practitioners. Because the overwhelming majority of this session is live, individual back-and-forth rather than conventional lectur e, Part I documents the session's format, purpose, and recurring patterns rather than pr esenting number ed doctrine, following the same appr oach used for prior live r oll-call sessions. In line with Ashaeiynn's own practice of not turning individual r eadings into an exhaustive public r ecor d, this document illustrates the pattern with a handful of r epr esentative examples rather than cataloguing every named practitioner's specific reading. This session contains substantial genuine live back-and-forth (r eadings, a live audience question, and closing devotional content), so it is pr ocessed as a full 3-part document.
1. Session Purpose and Format

Per this teaching, this session is dedicated to identifying each practitioner's kul devta or kul devi (the deity specifically tied to their family/ancestral lineage) — Bhaiya calls out names one at a time, asks whether the practitioner already knows their kul devta, then reveals or confirms it, along with a "tarang" (wave/ener gy) percentage reading indicating how strongly that deity's ener gy is currently active for them, and a recommended number of havans (fire rituals) to strengthen the connection.
2. Why This Session Took Priority Over the Chandravanshi Series

Per this teaching, Bhaiya explains that although the plan had been to continue the Chandravanshi series, he chose to prioritize this Kul Devta session instead, because delaying practitioners' pending prayers for their own ancestral connection would be a disservice, and because logistics that week (a session leader's planned time of f) made it important to complete this before that leader's absence.
3. Teaching: Why Deepak Pradajwalan (Lamp-Lighting) Matters — the Role of Shiv Tattva

Per this teaching, Bhaiya opens by explaining that over 5,000 lamps are regularly dedicated at the guru's feet on the day after every Purnima (full moon), as an ongoing, long-standing practice. Per this teaching, this is explained through Shiv tattva: when a practitioner ascends dimensions through agni vidya (fire-based practice), a powerful sur ge ("vega") is generated in the kundalini shakti, and Shiv tattva is what is needed to calm and regulate that sur ge — since agni tattva alone is "hard" (kathor) and every element carries both a positive and a controlling counterpart, the universe itself being fundamentally neutral.
4. Opening Prayer

Per this teaching's live practice, a formal prayer is of fered specifically invoking each practitioner's kul (ancestral lineage) shakti, asking that all Ram bhakts present be granted a direct encounter (sakshatkar) with their own kul devta's ener gy .
5. The Live Reading Format, Illustrated

Per this teaching's live practice, readings follow a consistent pattern. For example: one practitioner's kul devi was confirmed as Mata Kher Bhavani (a regional deity of Jammu & Kashmir), with a 6% tarang reading, described as indicating the family's worship has occurred but there is room to grow; another practitioner (previously unaware of their kul devta) was told it was Maa Dholagarh, a form of Maa Brahmacharini, with a strong 32% tarang reading, indicating regular family worship.
6. Tarang (Energy) Readings Vary Widely

Per this teaching, tarang readings given throughout this session ranged from as low as 0-3% (indicating little to no active family worship of the kul devta) up to 41-44% (indicating strong, sustained family devotion) — with most falling in a broad middle range, and each accompanied by a specific recommended number of havans (typically two to five) to strengthen the connection.
7. A Very Low Tarang Reading and Its Explanation

Per this teaching, when one practitioner (recently connected to Ashaeiynn) showed no active worship of the specific kul devi named (Mata Kali), and a resulting 0% tarang reading, Bhaiya immediately clarified this is temporary and correctable — of fering the reassurance "der aaye, durust aaye" (better late than never) alongside a firm caution not to let this drift further , since restoring a badly neglected kul devta connection becomes progressively harder the longer it is ignored.
8. Teaching: The Danger of Fully Forgetting One's Kul Devta

Per this teaching, Bhaiya states directly that when a person completely for gets their kul devta, tantriks and troublesome pitru influences can take advantage unchecked, and that person's life becomes marked by unusually severe, prolonged struggle — because, per this teaching's framing, "jo apne pita ko bhool gaya usko samagra roop se dev samaj bhool jaata hai" (one who for gets their own father is, in turn, for gotten by the whole divine community).
9. Teaching: Kul Devta Changes Across Differ ent Births

Per this teaching, in response to a live question, kul devta is tied to the specific family lineage a soul is born into in each life — meaning kul devta is not fixed across all of a soul's incarnations, and practitioners are expected to identify and respect the kul devta of whichever family they are presently born into, regardless of any prior life's lineage.
10. A Case Requiring Extended Remedial Practice

Per this teaching, one practitioner who had performed prior sadhna dedicated to her kul devi but had not yet completed the associated havan was instructed to complete that unfinished havan and sadhna fully rather than leaving it partially done, alongside continued lamp-lighting.
1 1. A Case of Pr olonged Complete Neglect

Per this teaching, one practitioner whose family had no active kul devi worship at all (beyond general temple visits) received a 0% tarang reading and was given an extended remedy: 90 days of an akhand deepak (continuously burning lamp) combined with six havans, with Bhaiya emphasizing this is achievable and that "der aaye, durust aaye" applies here as well.
12. Teaching: Pr esent Devotion Determines the Reading, Not Past Neglect

Per this teaching, across multiple readings, Bhaiya repeatedly notes that a practitioner's own recent sincerity and prayer — not just inherited family practice — visibly shapes these live readings, framing the accuracy of each identification as a direct reflection of the practitioner's own devotion rather than any special ability on his part.
13. Interludes of Warmth and Humor

Per this teaching's live texture, the roll call includes frequent lighthearted moments — technical/network interruptions handled with humor , playful teasing about names, and general warmth — alongside the more serious spiritual content, consistent with the community's blended tone of seriousness and genuine care.
14. A Note on Bhaiya's Dir ect Speaking Style

Per this teaching, Bhaiya of fers an aside acknowledging that his own regional (North Indian) manner of speaking can come across as blunt or overly direct compared to gentler regional speaking styles (which he contrasts with Middle India and South India), and asks that no one take personal of fense, attributing this to his own upbringing rather than any disrespect toward the deities or practitioners being addressed.
15. Closing: Transition to Prayer and Bhajan

Per this teaching's live practice, the Kul Devta session closes with a formal vandan (salutation) to the guru, followed by an extended personal prayer/bhajan sequence — a devotional song asking Hanuman ji for grace and a vision of Ram-Sita — reflecting on how , as a person ages, they increasingly recognize a higher power guiding their life rather than believing everything results from their own ef fort alone.
16. Closing Devotional Recitation

Per this teaching's live practice, the session closes with an extended devotional recitation, including verses in praise of Shri Ram (in the style of the Ram Rakshastotram/"Shri Ramchandra Kripalu") and a recitation of the Hanuman Chalisa, sung communally .
QUICK RULES SUMMARY

This session was dedicated specifically to identifying practitioners' kul devta/kul devi (family/ancestral deity) through live, individual "tarang" (ener gy) readings and recommended havan counts — prioritized this week ahead of continuing the Chandravanshi series. Regular lar ge-scale lamp-lighting (5,000+ lamps after every Purnima) is explained through Shiv tattva: it regulates the powerful sur ge generated in the kundalini shakti by agni-based practice, since every spiritual element carries both a positive and a controlling counterpart. Individual tarang readings in this session ranged from 0% (no active family worship) to over 40% (strong, sustained devotion), each paired with a specific recommended number of havans. A very low or 0% tarang reading is treated as correctable, not permanent — "der aaye, durust aaye" (better late than never) — but Bhaiya cautions against letting the connection drift to full neglect, since restoring it becomes progressively harder over time. Completely for getting one's kul devta is described as opening the door to unchecked tantrik and pitru interference and unusually severe, prolonged life struggle. Kul devta is tied to the specific family a soul is born into in each life — it is not fixed across all incarnations, and practitioners must identify and honor the kul devta of whichever family they are presently born into. A practitioner's own present sincerity and prayer , not just inherited family practice, is described as directly shaping these live readings. This session's core content is individual, live readings rather than conventional numbered doctrine, so Part I documents the session's format and patterns rather than an exhaustive list of each participant's specific reading. Spelling note: the institute's name is written "Ashaeiynn" — use this spelling consistently .
Part II — Q&A Pairs (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Q&A Pairs (Session 79, English)
A Live Kul Devta Roll Call: Identifying Family/Ancestral Deities, "T arang" Readings, and Why Kul Devta Must Never Be Forgotten

User-style questions with answers gr ounded in this Ashaeiynn live training session. Gr eeting style: "Jai Siyaram." Because this session consists almost entir ely of individual kul devta r eadings, these Q&A pairs focus on the session's general teaching content and r ecurring patterns rather than any specific individual's personal r eading.

Q1. What is a "Kul Devta Session," per this teaching? A: Per this teaching, it is a dedicated live session where Bhaiya identifies each practitioner's kul devta or kul devi (family/ancestral deity), confirms or reveals it, and gives a "tarang" (ener gy) percentage reading along with a recommended number of havans to strengthen that connection.

Q2. Why was this Kul Devta session prioritized over continuing the Chandravanshi series? A: Per this teaching, because delaying practitioners' pending prayers for their own ancestral connection would be a disservice, and because that week's logistics (a session leader's planned time of f) made it important to complete this session promptly .

Q3. Why is r egular large-scale lamp-lighting (thousands of lamps after Purnima) important, per this teaching? A: Per this teaching, it relates to Shiv tattva — when a practitioner ascends dimensions through agni-based (fire) practice, a powerful sur ge is generated in the kundalini shakti, and Shiv tattva is needed to calm and regulate that sur ge, since agni tattva alone is described as "hard," and every spiritual element carries both a positive and a controlling counterpart.

Q4. What does a "tarang" per centage r eading indicate? A: Per this teaching, it indicates how strongly a practitioner's kul devta's ener gy is currently active for them, generally reflecting how much genuine worship and devotion (past and present) has been directed toward that deity .

Q5. What range of tarang r eadings came up in this session? A: Per this teaching, readings ranged from as low as 0-3% (little to no active family worship) up to over 40% (strong, sustained devotion), with most practitioners falling somewhere in between.

Q6. Is a low or 0% tarang r eading tr eated as a permanent pr oblem? A: No — per this teaching, it is treated as correctable, summarized as "der aaye, durust aaye" (better late than never); however , practitioners are cautioned not to let the connection drift into full neglect, since restoring it becomes progressively harder over time.

Q7. What happens, per this teaching, when someone completely forgets their kul devta? A: Per this teaching, it opens the door to unchecked tantrik and pitru interference, and the person's life tends to be marked by unusually severe, prolonged struggle — described as being, in ef fect, for gotten by the wider divine community in turn.

Q8. Does a person's kul devta stay the same acr oss every lifetime? A: No — per this teaching, kul devta is tied to the specific family lineage a soul is born into in a given life; practitioners are expected to identify and honor the kul devta of whichever family they are presently born into, not a prior life's lineage.

Q9. What is typically r ecommended alongside havans for strengthening a kul devta connection? A: Per this teaching, regular lamp-lighting (diya) is consistently of fered as an accessible practice alongside havans — with an akhand deepak (continuously burning lamp) over an extended period (such as 90 days) recommended in cases of especially low tarang readings.

Q10. Does a practitioner's own effort matter , or is a r eading pur ely about inherited family practice? A: Per this teaching, a practitioner's own present sincerity and prayer visibly and directly shape these live readings — Bhaiya repeatedly frames the accuracy of each identification as a reflection of the practitioner's own devotion, not a special ability of his own.

Q1 1. If a family has not actively worshipped their kul devi for a long time, is ther e still hope for a str ong connection? A: Yes — per this teaching, even a practitioner whose family had no active kul devi worship at all was given a clear , concrete remedial path (an extended period of akhand deepak plus several havans), with the encouragement that recovery is achievable.
Bot Response Guidelines

Do not provide or speculate about any specific named practitioner's individual kul devta identity , tarang percentage, or recommended havan count from this session — respond only with the general patterns and teachings documented here. Present the tarang percentage system (Q4–Q6) as this teaching's own framework for describing spiritual connection strength, not as a claim of precise measurement. Keep the "kul devta changes across births" teaching (Q8) intact and specific — it applies to the family lineage of a given incarnation, not a claim that personal deity preference is arbitrary . Present the warnings about neglecting kul devta (Q7) matter -of-factly , without dramatizing or adding details beyond what this teaching states. Yeh exchange isliye include kiya gaya kyunki yeh dikhata hai ki Bhaiya kis tarah warmth aur seriousness dono ke saath r espond karte hain — na toh judgment, na toh panic, balki ek clear , achievable r emedial path ke saath encouragement.
Sangat (live sawaal poochte hue): भैया, हम हर जन्म में अलग-अलग जन्म लेते हैं तो कुल के देवता भी उसके िहसाब से बदल जाते हैं, िक वही रहते हैं?
Bhaiya: नहीं, आपके बदल जाते हैं, क्योंिक िजस कुल में तुम जन्म लोगे उस कुल के एक पिट�कुलर देवता होंगे। इसिलए तुम्हें हर उस कुल के देवता की िरस्पेक्ट करनी पड़ेगी िजस जन्म में तुम अपना अवतार ले रहे हो।

Yeh exchange isliye include kiya gaya kyunki yeh ek genuinely inter esting, universal spiritual question hai jo bahut practitioners ke man mein aata hoga — r eincarnation aur kul devta ke beech ka r elationship — aur Bhaiya ka jawab clear aur concise hai.

Bhaiya (apni dir ect boli ke baar e mein ek halka sa disclaimer dete hue): देिखए , हमारी जुबान है ना, यहां की थोड़ी सी खड़ी जुबान है — हम िजस भाव से बोलते हैं उस भाव से आप समझ जाइए, क्योंिक हमारे नॉथ� इंिडया में हम बहुत ज्यादा डायरेक्ट बोलते हैं। कभी-कभी हम माता को या िकसी भी शिक्त को एकदम तरीके से नहीं बोल पाते। तो कोई भी इस बात को अपने िदल पर ना ले।
